sample_unit: decision-tree model simulation (no patient sample reported)

links.outcome: Skin cancer detection rate and cost of AI app versus usual care
links.effect: App detection rate lower than usual care: melanoma 0.601 vs 0.874, BCC 0.585 vs 0.912, SCC 0.706 vs 0.922, benign 0.820 vs 0.937; costs were lower or similar; unnecessary benign referrals.
links.quote: In its current diagnostic performance the AI-based app was associated with lower skin cancer detection rates and as a consequence, lower costs.

unlisted_practices: Health economic (cost-effectiveness) evaluation of AI before reimbursement or implementation decisions

screen.reason: Economic decision-analytic simulation evaluating the cost-effectiveness and diagnostic pathway impacts of deploying the SkinVision AI app vs usual care.
